requirements: Watcher::new, serial, changed, drain_with_reader, version_with_reader and all original wrappers remain byte-exact in the Rust reference.
Actual inotify_init1/read/inotify_add_watch/inotify_rm_watch, real file metadata and clone/close boundaries; no fixture policy substitute in production.
HIA owns all serial/generation/dead/LRU/scope/error-selection/drain-budget policy. Mechanical bridge owns only real capability, memory, syscall, mutex/atomic and cleanup operations.
Exactly 64 read attempts and 16,384 processed events; Interrupted consumes an attempt, WouldBlock succeeds even on the last attempt; dense invalid tail is not processed after the event bound.
Directory event stream is parsed as full 16-byte inotify_event header plus event.len bytes, with exact source error precedence, full buffer and retained unused tail.
serial increments only on checked success below 2^63; overflow does not assign self.next. Every changed call consumes one serial even when no watch matches.
Version begins with drain. A drain error first calls changed(-1, IN_Q_OVERFLOW), which may override the error on serial exhaustion; partial successful state changes are retained.

Live identity hit removes then pushes the same watch to the LRU back, with no new pin/watch/id. A dead hit removes the watch, performs ignored rm_watch, then releases its old pin before creating a new pin.
shared_pin Some clones the actual existing Arc<File>, not its FD. None uses actual File::try_clone. Add-watch failure releases that new pin after capturing original errno.
After successful add_watch, serial failure drops the new pin but does not invent inotify_rm_watch; original code leaves that kernel watch until stream cleanup.
Eviction occurs only after new watch serial succeeds; old rm_watch errors are ignored, old pin is released, then the new Watch is appended.
Ordinary mask observes membership/self movement only; content adds MODIFY/CLOSE_WRITE/ATTRIB. Fingerprint fallback must not read payloads.

Global namespace mutex poison/init/version errors go through original version fallback; content mutex poison returns its exact error, new/version failure returns None and retries only when source does.
ContentWatchSet scope is 1..258 entries. Validate scope before NEXT fetch_update; consume set serial before inotify initialization, including later construction failure.
Set NEXT is a real shared atomic counter, Relaxed checked fetch_update below 2^63. Set high-bit identities never alias flat Watch ids.
Set construction uses real shared Arc pins for every directory, final drain, exact watch-count and dead checks; duplicate identities or incomplete scope return None with complete owned cleanup.
Set version uses one lock/drain for all members; any drain error or dead watch permanently sets invalid, and later calls return None without rearming.
Rust Watcher drop closes events before dropping the Watch deque's Arc pins. Native failure/disposal must preserve this order and never close caller-borrowed FDs.
Real same-tree original/native/off tests preserve actual event order and full raw records; source-owned drain callbacks are separate private protocol controls, not real-kernel evidence.
Namespace wrapper and store/cache/caller qualification stay false until actual composite invocation and independent complete evidence read pass.
scope: Actual persistent Linux namespace and content-version implementation, then archive/cache callers
